newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares up, more gains depend on Wall Street.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares up, more gains depend on Wall Street.

text.p: Danish share prices closed higher in a positive market on Thursday with dealers seeing further rises ahead if Wall Street held its present levels.
"If U.S. bonds, the Dow Jones and the dollar manage to finish unchanged, we'll have a good Friday here, the underlying trend is basically positive here," one dealer said.
The KFX top-20 index gained 0.86 point to close at 144.76, while the KFX March future rose 1.05 point to 145.45 with 200 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Sophus Berendsen B was much in demand, with 149,000 shares changing hands to close 37 crowns higher at 807.
The day's most traded paper was Tele Danmark, with just over 300,000 shares moving, to close only one crown up at 351 after peaking at 358 earlier in the day.
The Tele Danmark fall was sparked by profit-taking in Belgacom after it announced an improved first half 1996 result. The Danish telecoms group owns 16.5 percent of Belgacom.
Overall turnover for the day was 1.578 billion crowns.
